doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: John's recording, studio isolation and the Sam First album
summary: He talks about John's writing, recording alone with headphones and an upcoming quintet live album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What’s in the near future for you? John tells me that he’s got a recording coming up I believe.

Hopefully that’s going to happen because I love playing John’s music you know. John is an interesting study, Monk, because when we were kids he was always reading. And somewhere between “Popular Science,” “Popular Mechanics” and Sherlock Holmes, this is where John’s whole writing concept was formed and it’s amazing. Plus a love for all the same music that we grew up listening to.
There’s a really enjoyable video of one of his pieces and the recording and I think you’re in a room by yourself with headphones on. Does that take some getting used to?

Oh sure it does. Especially with a big band. You know you’re used to being in there and everybody feels everybody. You really want the band to feel what you’re doing but it’s just not practical anymore. Fortunately there’s lots of, we have a great engineer out here and there’s lots of great engineers, but the one we work with, Tally Sherwood, he has the ability of making it sound as if you’re in the same room together. That’s crucial.

But you know to answer your question which is what’s on the horizon, I’m actually getting ready, next weekend my quintet is doing a live album recording at a club called Sam First. Now Sam First is inaugurating with this project, their own record label. Sam First Records. So we’re going to be their first project so I’m excited about that. I’m writing for that and Bill Cunliffe is writing for that, so the band is excited about getting together and just playing again. It’s been so long. So that’s on the horizon. That’s coming right up.
